cands.name: Juan Alanis
cands.bio: Republican member of the California State Assembly for District 22 since December 2022. Before that he was a Stanislaus County Sheriff's sergeant, patrol watch commander, acting police chief and SWAT member. He earned a bachelor's degree from CSU Stanislaus in 2017.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists the Republican Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), IUOE Local 3 and Reform California among his 2026 endorsements and voter-guide recommendations.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions by Alanis on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay and pensions, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. The Ballotpedia page shows no list of bills he sponsored, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or land-use stances. We found no personal background beyond his career, education and birthplace.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says he was born in Modesto and grew up in neighboring Riverbank, where he attended Riverbank High School, then Modesto Junior College and CSU Stanislaus.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assembly member since December 2022. Earlier he had a long Stanislaus County Sheriff's Office career (sergeant, patrol watch commander, acting police chief, SWAT, school resource officer). He ran for county sheriff in 2018 and lost.
qual.why: He has prior legislative service, which puts him in the high band. His career is in law enforcement rather than law, policy or budget work, so he scores at the lower end of that band. Committee seats were not counted.
